findings.message: The child writes its whole result, now up to several MB, with a single fs.writeSync(1, ...). Writing to a pipe, writeSync can return having written only part of the string, or throw EAGAIN if the pipe is in non-blocking mode (Node may set that when process.stdout is used, for example by an answer's console.log) and the parent has not drained it yet. A short write loses the end marker so every case

The phone check measures #toast-root when no toast is showing. By then the 5 s toasts have expired and hidePopover() has run, so the root is a closed popover that is laid out only because redesign.css's .toast-root { display: flex } overrides the browser's display:none for closed popovers. If that rule is ever removed or scoped, getBoundingClientRect() returns zeros and the check fails with 'left
findings.evidence: const phone = JSON.parse(await evaluate('JSON.stringify((() => { const box = document.getElementById("toast-root").getBoundingClientRect(); const view = document.documentElement; return { left: Math.round(box.left), right: Math.round(view.clientWidth - box.right), bottom: Math.round(view.clientHeight - box.bottom) }; })())'));

findings.message: The child now prints each case's full JSON result, passing or not, where it used to print only 'ok' for a pass. execFile's maxBuffer is 1 MB for the whole run, so a correct answer whose results are large now fails every case with 'did not run' (reproduced: two correct 600 KB results, expected values equal, both report did not run). The verify route allows up to 256 KB of expected values, so only s

The results are parsed from the marker to the end of stdout, so anything the answer prints after the child's own line (for example a process.on('exit', ...) handler that logs) makes JSON.parse throw and every case scores 'no results' (reproduced: a correct function that logs 'bye' on exit scored 0). Print the marker again after the JSON and parse only between the last two markers, or cut at the cl

The forged exit line uses the old [[1,"ok"],...] shape. The parent now expects [kind, text] strings, so judgeCase rejects this line for being malformed and the test passes for that reason, not because forging cannot work. The property worth testing is that a well-formed forged line still needs the expected value: forge [["v", "<wrong text>"], ...] and assert 0, and keep the 'expected values never

runBenchmark with iterations: 0 throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toFixed)' (reproduced). summarizeStats returns a reduced object for an empty list (no cv, rSD or range), and formatStatsSummary then calls stats.cv.toFixed. The scripts always pass positive counts, but the function is exported and tested as a unit. Reject iterations below 1 with a clear error, or make the empty su

The run-only-as-a-script guard compares import.meta.url, which Node resolves to the real path, with process.argv[1], which is not resolved. Started through a symlink or junction, npm run perf:multistep exits 0 and prints nothing (reproduced with a junction to the project). Compare fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1]) instead; settings-perf.mjs has the same guard.

Any mean above 50 ms gets the io-bound tag, and the extreme-latency message says 'likely I/O bound', from the timing alone. For these scripts that is right for the fsync-dominated workflows but wrong for a slow CPU-bound one, and the report then lists it under ioBound. Call the tag slow, or tag io-bound only when the benchmark says it touches the disk.

writeJsonAtomic keeps a .bak beside the file, and the cleanup removes only the file, so every run of this test leaves duck-settings-version-bad-<pid>-<time>.json.bak in the OS temp directory (reproduced: several are there now). Write the file inside a mkdtemp directory and remove the directory, as tests/fs-atomic.test.js does.

findings.message: Everything that is not Linux or ARM is assumed to have SMT, including Node built for x64 running under Rosetta 2 on an Apple Silicon Mac: process.arch is x64 and platform is darwin, so an 8-core M-series machine gets 4 generation threads, the case the ARM branch was written to avoid. os.cpus()[0].model is available without a subprocess and, as far as I know, names Apple silicon even under Rosetta

The probe now answers up to 8 items twice per pass, wide and serial, greedy and sampled: 32 answers before the tune starts, four times the earlier cost. It cannot be cut short: a greedy-pass mismatch still runs the sampled pass although the verdict is already 'refuse', and a --budget that the probe alone exhausts is only noticed afterwards. Return as soon as a pass mismatches, and pass the budget
findings.evidence: parallelInfo.probe = await probeParallel({ evaluate, width: decision.n, items: ids, settings, sampled: { temperature: 0.7 }, seed: 42 });

findings.message: The test 'a tune probes up to eight items' asserts that an exported constant equals the number it is defined as, so it passes whatever tune-job.mjs does with it. What matters is that the probe is asked for PROBE_ITEMS items: stub probeParallel or run runTune with a fake engine and check items.length, or drop the test.

The guide gives an exact file count next to a rounded test count: '93 files'. The same session added a test file two commits later (94 now, with 827 tests), so the number was wrong within the same push and will drift on every added file. A reader checking it finds a mismatch in a document judges are told to follow. Drop the file count or say 'about 90 files', and keep the test count rounded.
findings.evidence: This runs about 800 hermetic unit and integration tests in 93 files. No model
